subject: Request failure chain: Sprintline latency + 5xx (exec attention)
messages:
From: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@sprintline.com>
To: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Spike in 5xx and latency on /v1/generate — urgent

Hi Rachel / Ben,

We're seeing a surge of 5xx responses and tail latency from the Redwood API starting ~14:40 PST. Our application error rate rose from 0.6% to ~8% and p95 latency jumped from 120ms to ~1.8s. A handful of requests return connection resets.

We attached a short span of client-side traces and a few failing request IDs. Can you confirm whether anything changed in routing or if you see any peering/DNS anomalies on your side?

We're in the middle of a payment peak window; this is blocking checkout for many users.

Attachments: client-trace-12345.json (trace sample), request-ids.txt

Thanks,
Alex Dunn
Head of SRE, Sprintline
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T15:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx and latency on /v1/generate — urgent

Forwarding Sprintline's alert — high error rate and big p95 spikes during checkout. Rachel, can you triage contract/priority and confirm if they should be escalated to Exec? Soojin, can infra take a look at VPC peering stats, DNS resolution times in us-west-2, and proxy logs for the time window? I suspect a NAT gateway or proxy queueing issue.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T15:36:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx and latency on /v1/generate — urgent

On Fri, Dec 3, 2026 at 3:18 PM ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Forwarding Sprintline's alert — high error rate and big p95 spikes during checkout...

We've pulled the relevant intervals. Quick summary:
- Evidence of increased DNS lookup latency from our edge to Sprintline's peer (us-west-2 region) between 14:35-15:10 PST.
- Our proxy fleet shows a backlog on a subset of instances (proxy-uw2-a1,a4) with connection resets to upstream model hosts.
- KV cache hit rates were steady; not a cache miss storm.
- VPC peering metrics show transient retransmits across the peering attachment that correlate with the error window.

I'm attaching sanitized proxy logs + a sampled tcpdump and a server-side trace (sprintline-logs-20261203.tgz, trace-request-12345.json). We're opening INF-2579 and assigning to infra.

Next steps I'm actioning:
1) Shift traffic away from the two affected proxies (in progress).
2) Increase egress concurrency on dedicated pools to reduce queueing.
3) Ask networking to validate MTU/path MTU and peer health.

I'll update in 20–30 mins.

— Soojin
Soojín Lee
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sprintline-logs-20261203.tgz (logs), trace-request-12345.json (server trace)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx and latency on /v1/generate — urgent

Thanks for the rapid triage, Soojin.

Network notes from infra:
- Confirmed packet retransmits and TTL anomalies on the VPC peering path to Sprintline's AS between 14:33–15:02 PST. We've escalated to cloud provider NOC; they report a hardware-failover event in their peering fabric that matches the timestamp.
- DNS: we saw elevated resolver latency from our regional forwarders to Sprintline's authoritative records — likely exacerbated by the peering event.
- Short-term mitigation: we routed Sprintline traffic via a secondary peering route and forced a TTL reset on affected proxies. Initial telemetry shows error rate dropping back under 1% and p95 falling towards baseline.

Marissa/Rachel: We should notify Sprintline that root cause appears to be a transient peering fabric failover on the cloud provider side that created DNS timeouts and proxy queueing; provide a succinct exec brief and the mitigations taken. Recommend offering a one-time credit for the payment-window impact.

I'll keep the ticket open until cloud provider provides full postmortem.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure
From: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@sprintline.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T09:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx and latency on /v1/generate — urgent

Alex —

Thank you for the rapid report and for sharing traces. Short update for your execs and ours:

What we found
- Root cause: transient hardware failover in the cloud-provider peering fabric affecting the VPC peering path to Sprintline's network (us-west-2). This caused packet retransmits and increased DNS resolution latency, which in turn caused proxy queueing and connection resets to upstream hosts.

What we did
- Rerouted Sprintline traffic to a secondary peering path within 18 minutes of detection.
- Evacuated traffic from affected proxy instances and increased egress concurrency to reduce queuing.
- Collected logs/traces and opened INF-2579; cloud provider NOC engaged and investigating a hardware failover.

Impact & compensation
- Error rate peaked at ~8% between 14:35–14:58 PST; we estimate ~6 minutes of elevated error rate materially affected checkout flows.
- We propose a one-time service credit equal to one day's expected usage for Sprintline's paid tier during the impacted window. Ben/Marissa — please coordinate the credit and customer comms.

Next steps
- We'll share the cloud provider postmortem when available and a sanitized timeline. INF-2579 remains open until full resolution.
- We're also scheduling a short post-incident call with Sprintline to review mitigations and next steps; Alex, please let us know availability this week.

Apologies for the disruption — we prioritize reducing recurrence and improving detection for peering and DNS cascades.

Best,
Rachel Kim
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

--
